hadiths.info_note: Grade: Agreed upon by Bukhari and Muslim. The research text notes that it also appears in Muslim; only the Bukhari report, for which an explicit number was given, is presented here.

hadiths.turkish_text: Religion is sincere counsel; it is sincerity.
hadiths.narrator: Tamim ad-Dari (may Allah be pleased with him)
hadiths.key_lesson: Religious devotion is lived through sincerity, loyalty and an honest way of life that inspires trust, rather than through showing off.
hadiths.info_note: Grade: Sahih. The continuation of the hadith explains that this sincerity is owed to Allah, His Book, His Messenger and the believers.

hadiths.turkish_text: The deed most beloved to Allah is performing salah (prayer) at its prescribed time.
hadiths.narrator: Abdullah ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him)
hadiths.key_lesson: The value of salah is shown not only in performing it, but also in observing its prescribed time and performing it with care.
hadiths.info_note: Grade: Agreed upon by Bukhari and Muslim. The research text notes that it also appears in Muslim; the Bukhari report, for which an explicit number was given, is presented here.

hadiths.turkish_text: The best of you are those who learn the Quran and teach it.
hadiths.narrator: Uthman ibn Affan (may Allah be pleased with him)
hadiths.key_lesson: One's connection with the Quran deepens not only through reading it, but also through learning it and passing it on to others.
hadiths.info_note: Grade: Sahih.

hadiths.turkish_text: None of you truly believes until they love for their brother what they love for themselves.
hadiths.narrator: Anas ibn Malik (may Allah be pleased with him)
hadiths.key_lesson: True iman requires wishing good for others, abandoning envy and being fair in brotherhood.
hadiths.info_note: Grade: Agreed upon by Bukhari and Muslim.

hadiths.turkish_text: A believing man should not hate a believing woman entirely; if he dislikes one of her traits, he will be pleased with another.
hadiths.narrator: Abu Hurairah (may Allah be pleased with him)
hadiths.key_lesson: In marriage, being able to see a spouse's good qualities instead of looking for faults preserves compassion and peace.
hadiths.info_note: Grade: Sahih.

hadiths.turkish_text: What is halal is clear, and what is haram is clear. Between them are doubtful matters whose ruling most people do not know.
hadiths.narrator: Nu'man ibn Bashir (may Allah be pleased with him)
hadiths.key_lesson: A believer tries to avoid not only what is clearly haram, but also doubtful matters that could wear down the heart.
hadiths.info_note: Grade: Agreed upon by Bukhari and Muslim.

hadiths.turkish_text: Allah is pure and accepts only what is pure.
hadiths.narrator: Abu Hurairah (may Allah be pleased with him)
hadiths.key_lesson: The blessing of worship is closely tied to earning and eating what is halal.
hadiths.info_note: Grade: Sahih. The continuation of the hadith explains that consuming what is haram can prevent a supplication from being accepted.

hadiths.turkish_text: The Messenger of Allah cursed the one who takes interest, the one who pays it, the one who records it and the one who witnesses it.
hadiths.narrator: Jabir ibn Abdullah (may Allah be pleased with him)
hadiths.key_lesson: Interest is a serious prohibition that extends beyond the one who takes it and the one who pays it to those who support it.
hadiths.info_note: Grade: Sahih.

hadiths.turkish_text: Charity does not diminish wealth. Whenever a servant forgives, Allah increases their honor.
hadiths.narrator: Abu Hurairah (may Allah be pleased with him)
hadiths.key_lesson: Giving and forgiving for Allah's sake may appear to diminish what one has, but in reality they bring blessing and honor.
hadiths.info_note: Grade: Sahih.

hadiths.turkish_text: O Allah! You are my Lord. There is no god but You. You created me, and I am Your servant. I remain faithful to my promise and covenant with You as much as I am able. I seek refuge in You from the evil of what I have done. I acknowledge Your blessings upon me, and I admit my sin. Forgive me, for no one forgives sins except You.
hadiths.narrator: Shaddad ibn Aws (may Allah be pleased with him)
hadiths.key_lesson: One of the most powerful forms of seeking forgiveness is to ask Allah for forgiveness while acknowledging His oneness, His blessings, and one's own shortcomings.
hadiths.info_note: Grade: Sahih. The research text notes that particular emphasis is placed on reciting this supplication in the morning and evening.

hadiths.turkish_text: Whoever says 'Subhanallahi wa bihamdihi' one hundred times in a day will have their sins forgiven, even if they are as abundant as the foam of the sea.
hadiths.narrator: Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)
hadiths.key_lesson: Short but regularly recited authentic words of remembrance keep the heart alive and nourish hope for forgiveness.
hadiths.info_note: Grade: Sahih.

hadiths.turkish_text: Whoever says 'La ilaha illallahu wahdahu la sharika lah, lahul-mulku wa lahul-hamdu wa huwa ala kulli shay'in qadir' one hundred times in a day earns a great reward and is protected from Satan that day.
hadiths.narrator: Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)
hadiths.key_lesson: Regularly repeating this remembrance of Allah's oneness is one of the powerful daily acts that bring reward, protection, and life to the heart.
hadiths.info_note: Grade: Sahih.

hadiths.narrator: Anas ibn Malik (may Allah be pleased with him)
hadiths.turkish_text: Whoever possesses these three qualities will taste the sweetness of iman: loving Allah and His Messenger more than anything else, loving someone only for Allah's sake, and hating to return to disbelief as much as being thrown into the Fire.
hadiths.key_lesson: The sweetness of iman is felt by placing Allah and His Messenger above everything else and directing one's love and hatred for Allah's sake.
hadiths.info_note: Grade: Agreed upon by Bukhari and Muslim.

hadiths.narrator: Anas ibn Malik (may Allah be pleased with him)
hadiths.turkish_text: None of you has complete iman until I am more beloved to him than his father, his child, and all people.
hadiths.key_lesson: Loving the Prophet ﷺ more than everyone else is one of the fundamental measures of the maturity of iman.
hadiths.info_note: Grade: Agreed upon by Bukhari and Muslim.

hadiths.narrator: Ibn Umar (may Allah be pleased with him)
hadiths.turkish_text: Modesty is part of iman.
hadiths.key_lesson: Modesty is a part of iman that keeps a person from sin and protects the heart.
hadiths.info_note: Grade: Agreed upon by Bukhari and Muslim.

hadiths.narrator: Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)
hadiths.turkish_text: Iman has more than seventy branches. The highest is La ilaha illallah, and the lowest is removing something harmful from the road.
hadiths.key_lesson: Iman is not merely a belief held in the heart; it is a complete way of life expressed through words, actions, and good character.
hadiths.info_note: Grade: Agreed upon by Bukhari and Muslim.

hadiths.narrator: Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)
hadiths.turkish_text: This religion is ease. Whoever makes the religion too difficult for themselves will be overcome by it.
hadiths.key_lesson: The religion teaches sustainable, balanced, and sincere worship, rather than excess that wears a person down.
hadiths.info_note: Grade: Sahih.

hadiths.narrator: Sufyan ibn Abdullah ath-Thaqafi (may Allah be pleased with him)
hadiths.turkish_text: Say, 'I believe in Allah,' then remain steadfast.
hadiths.key_lesson: Iman is preserved not merely through words, but by living with honesty and steadfastness.
hadiths.info_note: Grade: Sahih.

hadiths.narrator: Abbas ibn Abd al-Muttalib (may Allah be pleased with him)
hadiths.turkish_text: Whoever accepts and is content with Allah as Lord, Islam as religion, and Muhammad as Messenger tastes the sweetness of iman.
hadiths.key_lesson: Being content with Allah, Islam, and the Messenger of Allah turns iman into peace in the heart.
hadiths.info_note: Grade: Sahih.

hadiths.narrator: Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)
hadiths.turkish_text: On the Day of Judgment, one of the first people to be judged against will be a person who performed deeds to show off.
hadiths.key_lesson: A deed performed so that people will see it may lose its value in Allah's sight, even if it appears great outwardly.
hadiths.info_note: Grade: Sahih. This narration reminds us that the intention behind a deed will be examined before its outward appearance.

hadiths.narrator: Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)
hadiths.turkish_text: Allah said: I am as My servant thinks of Me.
hadiths.key_lesson: A servant should have hopeful and good expectations of their Lord, keeping the door of supplication and repentance open.
hadiths.info_note: Grade: Agreed upon by Bukhari and Muslim. Having good expectations means repenting and hoping for mercy, not relying on sin.

hadiths.narrator: Jabir ibn Abdullah (may Allah be pleased with him)
hadiths.turkish_text: Between a person and shirk and disbelief is abandoning salah.
hadiths.key_lesson: Salah is one of the clearest signs of a believer's identity; abandoning it leads a person to a very dangerous point.
hadiths.info_note: Grade: Sahih. Although scholars explain the hadith differently, they all agree that abandoning salah is an extremely serious danger.

hadiths.narrator: Malik ibn al-Huwayrith (may Allah be pleased with him)
hadiths.turkish_text: Pray as you have seen me pray.
hadiths.key_lesson: Salah should be learned and performed as the Prophet ﷺ taught it, rather than according to personal preference.
hadiths.info_note: Grade: Sahih.

hadiths.narrator: Ibn Umar (may Allah be pleased with him)
hadiths.turkish_text: Salah performed in congregation is twenty-seven degrees more virtuous than salah performed alone.
hadiths.key_lesson: Salah performed in congregation brings believers both greater reward and a spirit of unity.
hadiths.info_note: Grade: Agreed upon by Bukhari and Muslim.

hadiths.narrator: Aishah (may Allah be pleased with her)
hadiths.turkish_text: The two rak'ahs of Sunnah prayer before the morning prayer are better than the world and everything in it.
hadiths.key_lesson: Even Sunnah prayers that may seem small can be more valuable than the blessings of this world, so they should not be neglected.
hadiths.info_note: Grade: Sahih.

hadiths.narrator: Uthman ibn Affan (may Allah be pleased with him)
hadiths.turkish_text: Whoever builds a mosque for Allah, Allah will build something similar for them in Paradise.
hadiths.key_lesson: Contributing to the building of a mosque for Allah is a lasting good deed whose effects continue after death.
hadiths.info_note: Grade: Agreed upon by Bukhari and Muslim.

hadiths.narrator: Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)
hadiths.turkish_text: When the iqamah is called for the obligatory prayer, there is no prayer except the obligatory prayer.
hadiths.key_lesson: Once the iqamah for the obligatory prayer begins, priority is given to the obligatory prayer; one does not occupy oneself with another voluntary prayer.
hadiths.info_note: Grade: Sahih.

hadiths.narrator: Abu Musa al-Ash'ari (may Allah be pleased with him)
hadiths.turkish_text: Whoever performs the morning and afternoon prayers will enter Paradise.
hadiths.key_lesson: Maintaining the morning and afternoon prayers is one of the great deeds that lead a servant to Paradise.
hadiths.info_note: Grade: Agreed upon by Bukhari and Muslim.

hadiths.narrator: Anas ibn Malik (may Allah be pleased with him)
hadiths.turkish_text: Straighten your rows, for keeping the rows straight is part of completing the prayer.
hadiths.key_lesson: Keeping the rows straight during salah is a sign of unity and seriousness in worship as well as order.
hadiths.info_note: Grade: Agreed upon by Bukhari and Muslim.

hadiths.narrator: Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)
hadiths.turkish_text: When Ramadan comes, the gates of Paradise are opened, the gates of Hell are closed, and the devils are chained.
hadiths.key_lesson: Ramadan is a special season of worship in which mercy expands and worship becomes easier.
hadiths.info_note: Grade: Agreed upon by Bukhari and Muslim.

hadiths.narrator: Anas ibn Malik (may Allah be pleased with him)
hadiths.turkish_text: Eat suhoor, for there is blessing in suhoor.
hadiths.key_lesson: Suhoor is more than just a meal; it is an important preparation that brings blessing to the fast and keeps the Sunnah alive.
hadiths.info_note: Grade: Agreed upon by Bukhari and Muslim.

hadiths.narrator: Sahl ibn Sa'd (may Allah be pleased with him)
hadiths.turkish_text: People will remain upon good as long as they hasten to break the fast.
hadiths.key_lesson: Breaking the fast at its proper time is part of completing the act of fasting in a balanced way in accordance with the Sunnah.
hadiths.info_note: Grade: Agreed upon by Bukhari and Muslim.

hadiths.narrator: Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)
hadiths.turkish_text: Let none of you fast one or two days before Ramadan begins.
hadiths.key_lesson: The beginning and end of Ramadan are determined by sound criteria and the Sunnah, not by personal estimation.
hadiths.info_note: Grade: Agreed upon.

hadiths.narrator: Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)
hadiths.turkish_text: Whoever eats or drinks forgetfully while fasting should complete the fast, for Allah has fed them and given them drink.
hadiths.key_lesson: A person who eats or drinks forgetfully does not sin; Allah has forgiven this mistake and counted the fast as valid.
hadiths.info_note: Grade: Agreed upon.

hadiths.narrator: Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)
hadiths.turkish_text: Fast when you see the crescent, and celebrate Eid when you see it again.
hadiths.key_lesson: Acts of worship observed at prescribed times, such as Ramadan and Eid, are begun and completed on the basis of sound religious criteria.
hadiths.info_note: Grade: Agreed upon.

hadiths.narrator: Abdullah ibn Amr (may Allah be pleased with him)
hadiths.turkish_text: The fast most beloved to Allah is the fast of Dawud: he would fast one day and not fast the next.
hadiths.key_lesson: The most virtuous approach to voluntary worship is a balanced devotion that does not exhaust a person and can be sustained.
hadiths.info_note: Grade: Agreed upon.

hadiths.narrator: Abu Ayyub al-Ansari (may Allah be pleased with him)
hadiths.turkish_text: Whoever fasts Ramadan and then follows it with six days of Shawwal is like one who has fasted the entire year.
hadiths.key_lesson: Fasting six days in Shawwal after Ramadan strengthens consistency in worship.
hadiths.info_note: Grade: Sahih.

hadiths.narrator: Abu Mas'ud al-Badri (may Allah be pleased with him)
hadiths.turkish_text: The last two verses of Surah al-Baqarah are sufficient for whoever recites them at night.
hadiths.key_lesson: The last two verses of Surah al-Baqarah are a great blessing, allowing a person to end the night with the Quran and providing spiritual protection.
hadiths.info_note: Grade: Agreed upon.

hadiths.narrator: Abu Musa al-Ash'ari (may Allah be pleased with him)
hadiths.turkish_text: La hawla wa la quwwata illa billah is a treasure from the treasures of Paradise.
hadiths.key_lesson: This brief remembrance instills in the heart that true strength and help come only from Allah.
hadiths.info_note: Grade: Agreed upon. This remembrance teaches that strength and success are possible only through Allah's help.

hadiths.narrator: Abu Malik al-Ash'ari (may Allah be pleased with him)
hadiths.turkish_text: Purity is half of iman. Alhamdulillah fills the scale.
hadiths.key_lesson: When purity, remembrance and patience come together, they purify both the believer's body and inner life.
hadiths.info_note: Grade: Sahih.

hadiths.narrator: Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)
hadiths.turkish_text: A group that gathers to remember Allah is surrounded by angels and covered by mercy, and tranquility descends upon them.
hadiths.key_lesson: Gatherings where Allah is remembered are blessed settings in which tranquility descends upon hearts and divine mercy surrounds those present.
hadiths.info_note: Grade: Sahih.

hadiths.narrator: Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)
hadiths.turkish_text: Our Lord descends to the lowest heaven when the last third of the night remains and calls upon those who supplicate.
hadiths.key_lesson: The time before dawn is one of the most precious times for supplication, seeking forgiveness and sincere prayer.
hadiths.info_note: Grade: Agreed upon. The expression in the hadith emphasizes the value of the time before dawn; the believer makes use of this time for supplication and seeking forgiveness.

hadiths.narrator: Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)
hadiths.turkish_text: Allah has ninety-nine names. Whoever preserves them and lives by them will enter Paradise.
hadiths.key_lesson: Learning and understanding Allah's names enables a person to know their Lord and turn to Him with greater awareness.
hadiths.info_note: Grade: Sahih. The meaning here is not merely to count the names, but to understand them and reflect them in one's life.

hadiths.narrator: Samurah ibn Jundub (may Allah be pleased with him)
hadiths.turkish_text: The words most beloved to Allah are: Subhanallah, Alhamdulillah, la ilaha illallah and Allahu akbar.
hadiths.key_lesson: As the tongue remains engaged in remembrances beloved to Allah, the heart is purified and remains alive.
hadiths.info_note: Grade: Sahih.

hadiths.narrator: Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)
hadiths.turkish_text: Satan flees from the house in which Surah al-Baqarah is recited.
hadiths.key_lesson: A home in which the Quran is recited grows spiritually stronger; Surah al-Baqarah in particular offers special protection in this regard.
hadiths.info_note: Grade: Sahih.

hadiths.narrator: Aishah (may Allah be pleased with her)
hadiths.turkish_text: Gentleness beautifies whatever it is present in; when it is taken away, it leaves it ugly.
hadiths.key_lesson: Gentle and considerate conduct is a great moral principle that improves the outcome even in the most difficult matters.
hadiths.info_note: Grade: Sahih.

hadiths.narrator: Aishah (may Allah be pleased with her)
hadiths.turkish_text: Allah is gentle and loves gentleness, and He gives for gentleness what He does not give for harshness.
hadiths.key_lesson: Allah loves gentleness; kindness and gentle conduct can mend many things damaged by harshness.
hadiths.info_note: Grade: Sahih.

hadiths.narrator: Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)
hadiths.turkish_text: Beware of suspicion, for suspicion is the falsest of speech.
hadiths.key_lesson: Ill suspicion creates distance between people; a believer should avoid making hasty judgments about others.
hadiths.info_note: Grade: Agreed upon.

hadiths.narrator: Jabir ibn Abdullah (may Allah be pleased with him)
hadiths.turkish_text: Every good deed is charity.
hadiths.key_lesson: Every genuine act of goodness, beyond material assistance, also has the value of charity.
hadiths.info_note: Grade: Agreed upon.

hadiths.narrator: Shaddad ibn Aws (may Allah be pleased with him)
hadiths.turkish_text: Allah has prescribed excellence in all things.
hadiths.key_lesson: Awareness of excellence requires doing everything, from worship to daily interactions, with care, goodness and compassion.
hadiths.info_note: Grade: Sahih.

hadiths.narrator: Anas ibn Malik (may Allah be pleased with him)
hadiths.turkish_text: Make things easy and do not make them difficult; give glad tidings and do not drive people away.
hadiths.key_lesson: When teaching and putting religion into practice, one should adopt an approach that makes things easy, rather than harshness that drives people away.
hadiths.info_note: Grade: Agreed upon.

hadiths.narrator: Imran ibn Husayn (may Allah be pleased with him)
hadiths.turkish_text: Modesty is entirely good.
hadiths.key_lesson: Modesty is a fine moral quality that protects a person from evil and directs them toward good, rather than diminishing them.
hadiths.info_note: Grade: Sahih.

hadiths.narrator: Hudhayfah (may Allah be pleased with him)
hadiths.turkish_text: A person who carries tales will not enter Paradise.
hadiths.key_lesson: A person who carries tales and causes discord between people commits a grave sin that destroys trust in society.
hadiths.info_note: Grade: Agreed upon.

hadiths.narrator: Abdullah ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him)
hadiths.turkish_text: Insulting a Muslim is sinful disobedience, and fighting a Muslim is disbelief.
hadiths.key_lesson: Insulting a Muslim and fighting a Muslim are among the gravest actions that harm the bonds of brotherhood.
hadiths.info_note: Grade: Agreed upon.

hadiths.narrator: Ibn Umar (may Allah be pleased with him)
hadiths.turkish_text: If a person says to his brother, 'O disbeliever,' the accusation returns to one of them.
hadiths.key_lesson: Calling a Muslim a disbeliever without due care also exposes the speaker to a dangerous burden of sin.
hadiths.info_note: Grade: Sahih. Declaring someone a disbeliever is a very serious judgment; words spoken in anger without knowledge bring a grave burden of sin.

hadiths.narrator: Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)
hadiths.turkish_text: When Allah wills good for a servant, He afflicts them with hardship.
hadiths.key_lesson: Sometimes a hardship that befalls a person can turn into a blessing that purifies them and brings them closer to Allah.
hadiths.info_note: Grade: Sahih.

hadiths.narrator: Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)
hadiths.turkish_text: The world is the believer's prison and the disbeliever's paradise.
hadiths.key_lesson: A believer sees worldly life as a place to prepare for the Hereafter, rather than a place of unlimited comfort.
hadiths.info_note: Grade: Sahih. The hadith does not mean that a believer will never rejoice; it means that a believer should live while comparing the blessings of this world with the Hereafter.

hadiths.narrator: Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)
hadiths.turkish_text: Allah said: My mercy has surpassed My wrath.
hadiths.key_lesson: Allah's mercy is vast; however many faults a person has, they should not close the door to repentance.
hadiths.info_note: Grade: Agreed upon by Bukhari and Muslim.

hadiths.narrator: Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)
hadiths.turkish_text: Allah divided mercy into one hundred parts. He sent one part down to the world and kept ninety-nine for the Hereafter.
hadiths.key_lesson: All the mercy in this world is a very small reflection of Allah's infinite mercy.
hadiths.info_note: Grade: Agreed upon by Bukhari and Muslim.

hadiths.narrator: Jabir ibn Abdullah (may Allah be pleased with him)
hadiths.turkish_text: Let none of you die without thinking well of Allah.
hadiths.key_lesson: Even as death approaches, a servant should remain hopeful about their Lord and never despair of His mercy.
hadiths.info_note: Grade: Sahih. This hope is not complacency without action; it is turning to Allah's mercy together with repentance.

hadiths.narrator: Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)
hadiths.turkish_text: A servant commits a sin, then says, 'My Lord, forgive my sin.' Allah says, 'My servant knows that he has a Lord who forgives.'
hadiths.key_lesson: Whenever a servant falls, if they sincerely return to Allah, the door of repentance opens again.
hadiths.info_note: Grade: Agreed upon by Bukhari and Muslim.

hadiths.narrator: Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)
hadiths.turkish_text: If the believer knew the punishment with Allah, no one would hope for Paradise; and if the disbeliever knew His mercy, no one would despair.
hadiths.key_lesson: Servitude to Allah calls for a balance: taking His punishment seriously while never despairing of His mercy.
hadiths.info_note: Grade: Sahih.

hadiths.narrator: Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)
hadiths.turkish_text: May the person who lives to see both parents or one of them reach old age, yet does not attain Paradise, be disgraced.
hadiths.key_lesson: Serving one's aging parents is not a heavy burden but a great opportunity that opens the way to Paradise.
hadiths.info_note: Grade: Sahih.

hadiths.narrator: Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)
hadiths.turkish_text: No child can fully repay their father, unless they find him enslaved and set him free.
hadiths.key_lesson: Whatever a child does, they can never fully repay their parents for their efforts and sacrifices.
hadiths.info_note: Grade: Sahih. The effort involved in childbirth and raising a child in particular explains why the rights of parents are held in such high regard.

hadiths.narrator: Ibn Umar (may Allah be pleased with him)
hadiths.turkish_text: One of the highest forms of kindness is for a person to care for their father's friends.
hadiths.key_lesson: Loyalty to one's parents is a broad virtue that extends to caring for their friends after the parents have died.
hadiths.info_note: Grade: Sahih.

hadiths.narrator: Aishah (may Allah be pleased with her)
hadiths.turkish_text: Whoever raises daughters well and treats them kindly, they will be a shield for that person against the Fire.
hadiths.key_lesson: Treating daughters with mercy and justice and giving them a good education is a great means of salvation.
hadiths.info_note: Grade: Sahih.

hadiths.narrator: Abdullah ibn Amr (may Allah be pleased with him)
hadiths.turkish_text: This world is a temporary provision. The best of its blessings is a righteous wife.
hadiths.key_lesson: One of the greatest blessings in this world is a righteous wife who supports a person in their faith and life.
hadiths.info_note: Grade: Sahih.

hadiths.narrator: Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)
hadiths.turkish_text: A woman is married for four qualities: her wealth, lineage, beauty, and religion. Choose the one who is religious.
hadiths.key_lesson: The main measure that brings lasting peace to a marriage is not wealth or lineage, but faith and good character.
hadiths.info_note: Grade: Agreed upon by Bukhari and Muslim. The hadith does not disregard the other factors, but emphasizes that religious commitment should be the primary consideration for lasting peace.

hadiths.narrator: Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)
hadiths.turkish_text: If a man calls his wife to his bed and she does not come, and he spends the night angry, the angels curse her until morning.
hadiths.key_lesson: Taking each other's rights seriously in marriage is an important responsibility that protects family harmony.
hadiths.info_note: Grade: Sahih. This warning teaches spouses not to belittle the emotional and physical rights of marriage; it is meant to protect those rights, not to turn the relationship into one of oppression.

hadiths.narrator: Ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him)
hadiths.turkish_text: O young people, whoever among you can afford to marry should marry. For it is more effective in lowering the gaze and better at preserving chastity.
hadiths.key_lesson: For a young person who has the means to marry, marriage is the safest way to preserve chastity and guard the gaze.
hadiths.info_note: Grade: Sahih. For someone who cannot afford to marry, sawm (fasting) is recommended as a temporary means of protection that disciplines desire.

hadiths.narrator: Abu Shurayh al-Ka'bi (may Allah be pleased with him)
hadiths.turkish_text: A person whose neighbor is not safe from their harm will not enter Paradise.
hadiths.key_lesson: A person who harms their neighbor undermines the trust and mercy required by iman.
hadiths.info_note: Grade: Sahih.

hadiths.narrator: Abu Dharr (may Allah be pleased with him)
hadiths.turkish_text: When you cook soup, add more water to it, then remember your neighbors.
hadiths.key_lesson: Good neighborliness is often maintained not through great resources, but through small acts of sharing and thoughtfulness.
hadiths.info_note: Grade: Sahih.

hadiths.narrator: Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)
hadiths.turkish_text: No neighbor should prevent another from placing a piece of wood or a beam against their wall.
hadiths.key_lesson: The rights of neighbors include not only avoiding harm but also accommodating reasonable requests.
hadiths.info_note: Grade: Agreed upon by Bukhari and Muslim.

hadiths.narrator: Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)
hadiths.turkish_text: For a wealthy person to delay paying a debt is an injustice.
hadiths.key_lesson: A person who delays paying a debt despite being able to pay does more than commit a fault; they commit an injustice that violates another person's rights.
hadiths.info_note: Grade: Agreed upon by Bukhari and Muslim.

hadiths.narrator: Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)
hadiths.turkish_text: Whoever takes people's property intending to repay it, Allah helps them repay it; whoever takes it intending to destroy it, Allah destroys them.
hadiths.key_lesson: Allah helps the person who truly wants to repay a debt; the intention to deceive destroys blessings.
hadiths.info_note: Grade: Sahih.

hadiths.narrator: Abu al-Yusr (may Allah be pleased with him)
hadiths.turkish_text: Whoever gives a debtor more time or reduces part of the debt, Allah will shade them in His own shade.
hadiths.key_lesson: Making things easier for a debtor may be a means for Allah to make things easier for His servant on the Day of Judgment.
hadiths.info_note: Grade: Sahih.

hadiths.narrator: Ma'mar ibn Abdullah (may Allah be pleased with him)
hadiths.turkish_text: Whoever hoards goods has committed a sin.
hadiths.key_lesson: Hoarding what society needs and selling it when prices rise is not a gain, but a sin that harms society.
hadiths.info_note: Grade: Sahih.

hadiths.narrator: Ubadah ibn as-Samit (may Allah be pleased with him)
hadiths.turkish_text: Gold exchanged for gold and silver for silver must be equal in amount and exchanged on the spot; whoever takes more has engaged in riba.
hadiths.key_lesson: To avoid riba, attention must be paid to the requirements of fairness, equality, and immediate exchange when exchanging similar goods.
hadiths.info_note: Grade: Sahih. The hadith does not permit manipulation of quantities or payment terms when exchanging goods of the same kind, so as to close the paths to riba.

hadiths.narrator: Ibn Umar (may Allah be pleased with him)
hadiths.turkish_text: The upper hand is better than the lower hand. The upper hand is the one that gives, and the lower hand is the one that asks.
hadiths.key_lesson: A believer strives to be the hand that gives whenever possible and does not burden others, rather than one that constantly asks.
hadiths.info_note: Grade: Agreed upon by Bukhari and Muslim.

hadiths.narrator: Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)
hadiths.turkish_text: Every morning two angels descend. One asks for the person who gives to be compensated, and the other asks for the miser to be destroyed.
hadiths.key_lesson: Wealth spent in Allah's cause does not diminish; miserliness causes blessings to be withdrawn.
hadiths.info_note: Grade: Agreed upon by Bukhari and Muslim.

hadiths.narrator: Adiyy ibn Hatim (may Allah be pleased with him)
hadiths.turkish_text: Protect yourselves from the Fire, even with half a date.
hadiths.key_lesson: Even a seemingly small act of charity, when given sincerely, can become a great good that protects a person from the Fire.
hadiths.info_note: Grade: Agreed upon by Bukhari and Muslim.

hadiths.narrator: Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)
hadiths.turkish_text: The best charity is that which a person gives from what is beyond their needs.
hadiths.key_lesson: When giving charity, a person should be generous while also not neglecting those they are responsible for supporting.
hadiths.info_note: Grade: Agreed upon. This balance also teaches a person not to leave their family in need when giving charity.

hadiths.narrator: Abu Hurayrah (r.a.)
hadiths.turkish_text: Whoever begs from people to increase their wealth is in fact asking for a piece of burning coal.
hadiths.key_lesson: Making a habit of begging when there is no real need harms a person's dignity and their hereafter.
hadiths.info_note: Grade: Sahih.

hadiths.narrator: Abu Hurayrah (r.a.)
hadiths.turkish_text: Charity is due every day for every joint in a person's body.
hadiths.key_lesson: Charity is not given only through money; kind words and helpful actions performed each day also count as charity.
hadiths.info_note: Grade: Agreed upon.

hadiths.narrator: Ibn Umar (r.a.)
hadiths.turkish_text: All of you are shepherds, and all of you are responsible for those under your care.
hadiths.key_lesson: Every person is responsible for others in their position; authority and responsibility go hand in hand.
hadiths.info_note: Grade: Agreed upon.

hadiths.narrator: Abu Musa al-Ash'ari (r.a.)
hadiths.turkish_text: A believer is like a building to another believer; they support one another.
hadiths.key_lesson: Believers should stand together like a building whose parts support one another.
hadiths.info_note: Grade: Agreed upon.

hadiths.narrator: Abu Hurayrah (r.a.)
hadiths.turkish_text: The bankrupt person of my community is one who comes with salah, sawm and zakat, but has insulted one person, slandered another, consumed another's wealth, shed another's blood and struck another.
hadiths.key_lesson: Violating the rights of others is so serious that it can exhaust your good deeds in the hereafter, even if you have performed many acts of worship.
hadiths.info_note: Grade: Sahih. Even the rewards of salah, sawm and charity can be transferred to those whose rights were violated; therefore, violating others' rights requires making amends as well as repentance.

hadiths.narrator: Abu Hurayrah (r.a.)
hadiths.turkish_text: On the Day of Judgment, rights will surely be restored to their owners; even the hornless sheep will receive its due from the horned sheep.
hadiths.key_lesson: No injustice is lost in Allah's sight; even the smallest wrong will surely receive its due.
hadiths.info_note: Grade: Sahih.

hadiths.narrator: Sa'id ibn Zayd (r.a.)
hadiths.turkish_text: Whoever unjustly takes a handspan of land will have seven layers of earth placed around their neck on the Day of Judgment.
hadiths.key_lesson: Unjustly taking another person's property or land is a grave injustice with severe consequences.
hadiths.info_note: Grade: Agreed upon.

hadiths.narrator: Abdullah ibn Mas'ud (r.a.)
hadiths.turkish_text: The first matter to be judged between people on the Day of Judgment will be bloodshed.
hadiths.key_lesson: One of the first matters to be reckoned with on the Day of Judgment will be lives unjustly taken.
hadiths.info_note: Grade: Agreed upon.

hadiths.narrator: Abu Hurayrah (r.a.)
hadiths.turkish_text: Whoever has wronged their brother concerning his property or honor should seek his pardon today, before the day comes when there will be no gold or silver.
hadiths.key_lesson: When one has violated another person's rights, one should not leave the matter until the hereafter, but should seek forgiveness and make amends today.
hadiths.info_note: Grade: Sahih. It is easy to seek forgiveness in this world while one has money and means; in the hereafter, payment will be made from one's good deeds.

hadiths.narrator: Ibn Mas'ud (r.a.)
hadiths.turkish_text: Paradise is as close to any one of you as the strap of their sandal, and so is Hell.
hadiths.key_lesson: What brings a person closer to Paradise or Hell may sometimes be a small action that is considered insignificant.
hadiths.info_note: Grade: Sahih. The hadith reminds us that every good and evil deed has a consequence, whether great or small.

hadiths.narrator: Anas ibn Malik (r.a.)
hadiths.turkish_text: The person destined for Hell who lived the most comfortable life in this world will be dipped into Hell once and will say that they never experienced any comfort.
hadiths.key_lesson: Comfort in this world is temporary; the true measure is the end a person will face in the hereafter.
hadiths.info_note: Grade: Sahih.

hadiths.narrator: Abu Hurayrah (r.a.)
hadiths.turkish_text: Your fire in this world is only one of seventy parts of the fire of Hell.
hadiths.key_lesson: Reflecting on the magnitude of the punishment of Hell keeps the heart alert and mindful of sin.
hadiths.info_note: Grade: Agreed upon.

hadiths.narrator: Abu Hurayrah (r.a.)
hadiths.turkish_text: The first group to enter Paradise will be radiant like the moon on the night of the full moon.
hadiths.key_lesson: Descriptions of Paradise awaken longing for the hereafter and eagerness for righteous deeds in the believer's heart.
hadiths.info_note: Grade: Agreed upon.

hadiths.narrator: Aishah (r.a.)
hadiths.turkish_text: People will be gathered on the Day of Judgment barefoot, naked and uncircumcised.
hadiths.key_lesson: Reflecting on the reality of the gathering on the Day of Judgment humbles worldly pride and calls a person to prepare for their reckoning.
hadiths.info_note: Grade: Agreed upon.

hadiths.narrator: Ubadah ibn as-Samit (r.a.)
hadiths.turkish_text: Whoever loves to meet Allah, Allah loves to meet them.
hadiths.key_lesson: For a believer who is preparing through righteous deeds, death is not the end of existence but the moment of meeting their Lord.
hadiths.info_note: Grade: Agreed upon.

hadiths.narrator: Jarir ibn Abdullah (r.a.)
hadiths.turkish_text: You will see your Lord as clearly as you see this moon; you will not crowd one another to see Him.
hadiths.key_lesson: Seeing Allah in Paradise is the greatest and most exalted blessing for a believer.
hadiths.info_note: Grade: Agreed upon. The comparison describes the clarity of the sight; it does not mean that Allah is likened to His creation.

hadiths.narrator: Ibn Mas'ud (r.a.)
hadiths.turkish_text: Envy is permitted only in the case of two people: one who spends their wealth in the cause of truth, and one who judges and teaches with wisdom.
hadiths.key_lesson: Lives worthy of admiration are those of people who benefit others through their knowledge and spend their wealth in the cause of truth.
hadiths.info_note: Grade: Agreed upon.

hadiths.narrator: Abu Bakrah (r.a.)
hadiths.turkish_text: Let those present convey this to those absent. Many a person to whom the message is conveyed understands it better than the one who heard it.
hadiths.key_lesson: Treating the correct knowledge one hears as a trust and conveying it to others is one of the main ways knowledge spreads.
hadiths.info_note: Grade: Sahih. Therefore, reliable knowledge should be preserved and conveyed accurately.

hadiths.narrator: Abu Hurayrah (r.a.)
hadiths.turkish_text: Whoever calls others to guidance will receive a reward equal to the rewards of those who follow them.
hadiths.key_lesson: Calling people to what is right brings a continuing reward equal to the rewards of those who do that good.
hadiths.info_note: Grade: Sahih.

hadiths.narrator: Abu Mas'ud al-Ansari (r.a.)
hadiths.turkish_text: Whoever guides someone to a good deed will receive a reward equal to that of the person who does it.
hadiths.key_lesson: Helping bring about a good deed is as valuable and rewarding as doing it oneself.
hadiths.info_note: Grade: Sahih.

hadiths.narrator: Abu Hurayrah (r.a.)
hadiths.turkish_text: If Satan comes to one of you and eventually asks, 'Who created your Lord?' let that person seek refuge in Allah and stop pursuing the thought.
hadiths.key_lesson: Satanic whispers are extinguished by stopping the discussion and seeking refuge in Allah, rather than pursuing them.
hadiths.info_note: Grade: Agreed upon. Continuing to argue with these whispers makes them grow; the best course is to seek refuge in Allah and direct one's mind elsewhere.
